outline.name: Private Pilot for Airplane Category Airman Certification Standards (ASEL knowledge elements)
outline.notes: Scope: knowledge (K) elements of every FAA-S-ACS-6C task that applies to an airplane single-engine land (ASEL) applicant, since the PAR knowledge test reports missed questions by ACS element code. Excluded: Task I.I (seaplane), I.G.K1k water rudders (ASES, AMES), II.E taxiing and sailing (ASES, AMES), IV.G through IV.L confined area, glassy water, and rough water (ASES, AMES), IX.E through IX.G and all of Area X (AMEL, AMES), XII.B seaplane post-landing (ASES, AMES), and elements the ACS marks [Archived] (VIII.E.K1a-d, IX.C.K1a-d). Where a K element prints lettered sub-items, each sub-item is its own objective and the lead-in stem is not listed separately; the exceptions are PA.I.D.K1, which carries content of its own beyond its single sub-item K1a (EFB) so both are listed, and VIII.E.K1 and IX.C.K1, whose sub-items are all archived so the parent stands alone. The ACS repeats some elements word for word across tasks (for example IV.A/C/E K1-K3, IV.B/D/F K1-K3, VII.B/C K1, K2, K4, and VIII.A-D K1a-d); each keeps its own ID because the knowledge test codes to each one, so expect identical match lists there. Risk management (R) and skill (S) elements are left out for now; R elements can be added later with IDs like PA.I.A.R1. Task mapping: Area I tasks map to I.A..I.H, Area III tasks to III.A and III.B, every other area to its area code. meta.js has no code for Area X (multiengine), which is out of scope, so nothing needed a closest-fit mapping. Text fields are plain-word paraphrases, not ACS wording. Currency: the ACS PDF read is the November 2023 edition (effective 2024-05-31); not re-checked against faa.gov for a newer change notice beyond the file served on the read date.
